Builds depend on their source alone: the file version follows Version (9.1.864.0) instead of the build's minute, which made every command-line build in a new minute recompile every project (the solution built again a minute later: 16 s and nothing compiled, against 134 s). The commit stays in the informational version (9.1.864+<commit>). UpdateProjectVersion leaves the publish scripts: it wrote the same stamp into a csproj's FileVersion, and no csproj carries a Version any more.

Client split, D - the heads isolated: an app head compiles against the app's side alone, a VPN service head against Core's, and a head that runs both halves in one process makes both. IInProcessVpnServiceFactory, IInProcessVpnService and the two factories go, with their parameter from WindowsDesktopHost.Run and LinuxDesktopHost.Run down to the devices: WindowsDevice and LinuxDevice start their VPN host alone. WindowsInProcessDevice (VpnServices.Host.WindowsTun) is a WindowsDevice whose start makes a WindowsVpnService in its process, for AvaloniaUI.Dev and for a MAUI app on Windows, which hands it to AppUi.Hosting.Maui's init. dev starts the VPN host as the daemon does, without --daemon: its kill switch lets out no service, and its first lines go to vpn-host.log. A desktop head references its VPN host with ReferenceOutputAssembly false, marked VhAppVpnHost, so a restore and a build take it first and nothing compiles against it; VpnHood.AppUi.Hosting.Desktop.Daemon's targets (buildTransitive) refuse the mark without ReferenceOutputAssembly false and place the VPN host's whole output beside the app's - its build's for a build, its own publish for a publish, with the app's configuration, runtime and self-containment - and fail the build on a file both carry with different content. The Windows VPN host heads target the app head's framework (net11.0-windows10.0.26100.0), as SQLitePCLRaw gave the two different builds under one name. The iOS and tvOS app heads reference their extension with ReferenceOutputAssembly false too: the engine's 13 assemblies leave the app's compile references and its folder, and the extension keeps them. Docs: client-architecture.md, linux/README.md; CHANGELOG.Packages.md's Breaking lines. Checked: the solution builds; no desktop app head's compile references hold the engine or a host; the Windows and Linux publishes carry the same files as before; a setup on Windows 11 and an update on Ubuntu 26.04 connect, reconnect and disconnect, the daemon's stop ending its VPN host; dev starts and ends its VPN host; the iOS and tvOS heads build and start on the simulator; AppLib.Test, VpnHood.Test, AppUi.SmokeTest.

Client split, B - the move, no behavior change: each OS's VPN service leaves its device project for a project of its own, VpnHood.Core.Client.VpnServices.Host.<OS> (Android, Ios, Linux, WindowsTun, WindowsVpnPlugin), which references the device project; the device project keeps the app's half and what both halves share (folders and names, the VPN host's arguments, the kill switch, the system logger). The Store's activation component, its VPN service and its listener are one project, VpnServices.Host.WindowsVpnPlugin, the service and the listener internal there, as every public type of a C#/WinRT component must be a WinRT one; the package manifests' class names and Publish-WinStoreApp.ps1 follow. AppUiContext, PartialIntentScope and IWindowHandleUiContext move to AppLib.Abstractions; IosMemory is public, for the extension's monitor. No app-side project reaches Core.Client, Core.Tunneling or a VPN service host (AppLib.App.WindowsTun: 21 projects, from 29). Docs: client-architecture.md (new), README.md, source-layout.md, linux/README.md, the iOS docs; CHANGELOG.Packages.md's Breaking line. Checked: every head built (Android, iOS and tvOS on the Mac, both desktops, the Store package); AppLib.Test, VpnHood.Test, AppUi.SmokeTest; Android's VPN service on the emulator; the Store's VPN plug-in on Windows 11; a VPN host's connect on Windows 11 and Ubuntu 26.04.

Client split, A - the app's half and the VPN service's half untangled in place, no file moved yet: the device side stops naming the VPN service's types. The in-process VPN service is handed in, IInProcessVpnServiceFactory in Devices.Abstractions with WindowsVpnServiceFactory and LinuxVpnServiceFactory beside the services, through WindowsDesktopHost.Run and LinuxDesktopHost.Run, AvaloniaUI.Dev and AppUi.Hosting.Maui's init. Android starts its VPN service by the Java name it shipped under (AndroidDevice.VpnServiceJavaName, crc64198439f88d18e1a7.AndroidVpnService), with VpnServiceProcessName, VpnServiceActionConnect and its folders on the device. The VPN host's arguments live in one device-side type, WindowsVpnHostArgs and LinuxVpnHostArgs, --service becoming --daemon. The Store's app-service names (WindowsVpnPluginAppService), its connect timeout (WindowsVpnPluginDevice.PluginConnectTimeout) and its live profiles (TryGetLiveProfiles) move to its device project. What both halves share turns public.
